text:
alyssa: quick heads-up — ran the paged/flashed L2-stitch experiment on the 80GB node. seeing a large L2 write bandwidth spike around token 6k-8k that's correlated with pipeline stage 2 -> stage 3 handoff. attaching perf notes below. anyone else hit this when prefetch enabled?

mike: can you paste the kernel selection log? curious which variant was chosen for the long seq case. also what's batch size?

alyssa: batch=4, seq=8192 typical, router picked: flashfused (seq<=2048) -> paged-stitch (seq>2048). kernel log: ```kernel_select: FLASHFUSED v2 (path A) fallback FIREPAGED-STITCH (path B) selected_variant=FIREPAGED-STITCH kernel_idx=23 reason=occupancy_est>0.75```

sam: hmm the handoff geometry's known to spike sharedmem thrash if tile size doesn't match pipeline window. can you paste the perf counters around the spike? esp L2 evict rate + TLB misses.

alyssa: perf snippet (summarized): ```L2_READ_BW=18.2GB/s L2_WRITE_BW=12.8GB/s L2_EVICT_RATE=4.1k/s TLB_MISS=1.2k/s smem_bank_conflicts=23%``` looks like writes and evictions jump when the KV-cache streaming starts to replace prefix pages.

mike: that smem_bank_conflicts number is suspicious. are we using the 256-tile for the stitch path? last time we saw similar it was because the pipeline didn't insert the prefetch barrier early enough, letting stage3 stomp stage2's shared buffers. try reducing tile to 128 and add an extra pipeline fence before KV swap.

sam: +1. also try toggling the router heuristic threshold: bump the 'stitch_prefetch_seq_threshold' from 2048 -> 4096 so smaller long sequences still use fused path. could avoid the paged path for many mid-length requests. quick patch example (for testing only): ```{"stitch_prefetch_seq_threshold":4096, "max_prefetch_inflight":2}```

alyssa: updated a local config and reran microbench. results: L2_WRITE_BW fell to 7.4GB/s, eviction rate down to 1.1k/s, latency p95 improved ~18%. but overall throughput slightly worse for extreme-long streams (seq>12k) because fused path OOMs.

perf-bot: nightly microbench run 1957654300 completed. artifacts uploaded: s3://perf-artifacts/1957654321/l2-stitch/trace.json.gz

mike: can you run with nvprof counters + 'kvcache_pressure=low' flag and re-run the failing long seq? also collect nvlink counters if on multi-gpu. want to see whether the evictions are L2-local or result of cross-GPU prefetch noise.

alyssa: scheduling run now with nvprof + kvcache_pressure=low. ETA ~30m. I'm also patching tiled-smem to use asymmetric banks to reduce conflict (%) — small change but cheap to test.

sam: if that helps, we should add an automated heuristic to the kernel selector: if smem_bank_conflicts>15% and seq>4096 prefer fused path regardless of occupancy estimate. sounds hacky but will buy us stability while we tune pipeline fences.

mike: agreed. open a quick PR with the guard and a unit test using our microbench trace as input. label as "experimental". also add a perf regression alert so we don't ship without noticing.

alyssa: will do. uploading logs and a short write-up to the perf board when runs finish. thanks all. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: build #4521 for branch l2-stitch-prefetch started (tests: small, microbench). link: https://ci.internal/redwood/builds/4521

sam: one more note — check kernel memory allocator for small alignment frag. last run showed a 64-byte misalign that increases smem bank conflict under specific tiling. if present, a single-line align fix dropped conflicts by ~6%.

alyssa: noted, adding allocator align check to the run. will post follow-up thread with final numbers.
